content: Desloratadine is prescribed to alleviate symptoms of hay fever and other allergies, such as sneezing, a runny nose, and red, itchy, or watery eyes. It is also used to treat hives. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as antihistamines. It works by blocking histamine, a substance in the body responsible for causing allergic symptoms. Compared to other antihistamines, desloratadine is less likely to cause drowsiness. Desloratadine is available as a tablet and an orally disintegrating tablet, both of which are taken by mouth. It is typically taken once daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take desloratadine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. To take the orally disintegrating tablet, ensure your hands are dry before peeling back the foil packaging. Remove the tablet immediately and place it on your tongue. The tablet will dissolve quickly and can be swallowed with saliva. Orally disintegrating tablets can be taken with or without water. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking desloratadine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to desloratadine, loratadine (Claritin), or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease or phenylketonuria (PKU), especially if you are using the orally disintegrating tablets. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking desloratadine, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Desloratadine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: headache, upset stomach, dizziness, sore throat, dry mouth, muscle pain, extreme tiredness, or painful menstruation. Although rare, some side effects can be serious. If you experience difficulty breathing, contact your doctor immediately. If you notice any unusual problems while taking this medication, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
